sentences.text:
This Criminal Petition under Sections 480 and 483 of B.N.S.S.,
has been filed by the petitioner/Accused, seeking regular bail in
Cr.No.324/2025 of Iv Town Police Station, Visakhapatnam District.

2. The above said crime was registered against the
petitioner/Accused herein for the offence punishable u/Secs. 318(4), 69
of Bns.
3.

In brief, it is the case of prosecution that on 20.12.2024, the
complainant/victim Koralana Anitha turned up to police station and
lodged a written report duly stated that, she is the home maker and her
husband working in Visakha Container Terminal. On 28.04.2024 she
along with her husband and daughter went to beach on the occasion of
their marriage day, while she sat separately due to some disputes with
her husband.

On that one Sankar who is their relative came along with
another person and wished her.

Later, the other person introduced
himself as a Pastor i.e. accused who observed her distress and told her
that there were some evil spirits in her soul and her house.

He further
 2

gave an advice that, if she believes in Jesus, all her problems would be
vanished.

Later, he got acquaintance with her and occasionally visited
their home to pray and offered her that if she believes in Jesus Christ,
he would arrange any job to her.

Later, he participated in sexual
intercourse to release her difficulties/stress, so that she would be
blessed with god's grace.

Later, he forcefully had sexual intercourse with
her in the absence of her family members.

Later, he took her to
Jalaripeta and kept her in a house with a promise that he would marry
her if necessary and took her gold ring and cash of Rs.10,000/- and took
a rented house at P.M.Palem where he had sexual intercourse with her
and later started harassing her.

During his absence, she escaped from
said place and went to her parental home at Burma colony and revealed
entire episode what was happened and now she lodged this complaint
against the accused for taking necessary action in accordance with the
law.

4. Heard and perused the record.
5.

The learned counsel for the petitioner submits that the petitioner
has been in judicial custody since 03.02.2025.

A reading of the report
reveals that the de facto complainant/victim is a married woman, and

the
petitioner is known to her.

According to the contents of the report, the
petitioner made her believe that if she had a physical relationship with
him, all the problems in her body and household would be resolved, and
 3
she would live happily.

The report further suggests that she is residing
with her husband and children.

The learned counsel for the petitioner

further submits that the petitioner has been in judicial custody for more
than 90 days.

6. The learned Assistant Public Prosecutor submits that a primary
charge sheet has been filed, completing most of the investigation.

The
learned Assistant Public Prosecutor

, while opposing the prayer of the
petitioner/accused, submits that the investigation is not yet complete.

Upon inquiry, the learned Assistant Public Prosecutor confirmed that the
petitioner has no criminal antecedents.

7. This Court, without going into the submission made by the learned
counsel for the petitioner regarding the applicability of Section 69 of the
Bns (Section 376 of the Ipc), finds that further detention of the
petitioner is no longer required for conducting further investigation.

Therefore, this Court is inclined to grant bail to the petitioner/accused,
subject to the following conditions:
 (i) The petitioner/accused herein shall be released on his
 executing a personal bond for Rs.25,000/- (Rupees twenty
 five thousand only) with two sureties for a like sum each to
 the satisfaction of the learned Vi Additional District &
 Sessions Judge, Visakhapatnam;
 4
 (ii) On release, the petitioner/accused shall appear before
 the Station House Officer concerned on every Sunday
 between 10.00 a.m. and 1.00 pm for a period of three (03)
 months.

(iii) The petitioner/accused shall not tamper with the
 evidence and hamper the investigation and shall cooperate
 for investigation.
8. Accordingly, the Criminal Petition is allowed.
